title: Lewis Dot Structures of Common Compounds
notes: **Lewis structure rules:** count total valence electrons, draw skeleton, distribute electrons to satisfy octets, place remaining electrons on central atom, form double/triple bonds if needed.
**Formal charge:** $FC = V - N - B/2$, where $V$ is valence electrons, $N$ is non-bonding electrons, $B$ is bonding electrons. The best structure minimizes formal charges.

**Examples:** NaCl (ionic: Na$^+$ [Ne] and Cl$^-$ [Ar]); $H_2O$ (O with two lone pairs, two O-H bonds, bent shape); $CO_2$ (O=C=O, linear); $NH_3$ (N with one lone pair, three N-H bonds, trigonal pyramidal).
**Expanded octet:** elements in period 3 and beyond can have more than 8 electrons because they have d-orbitals available. Example: $SF_6$ has 12 valence electrons around S.
**Odd-electron molecules:** NO has 11 valence electrons, giving an unpaired electron and a doublet state. These are paramagnetic and reactive.
